camera_terms.definition: A framing in which the subject is very small within an expansive environment.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Environment dominates and scale relationships become explicit.
camera_terms.use_when: Establish geography, spectacle or overwhelming scale.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that shows the complete subject with substantial surrounding space.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Body, action and environment remain readable together.
camera_terms.use_when: Show a subject in meaningful surroundings.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that contains a standing subject from head to feet with limited margin.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The whole body is legible without letting the setting dominate.
camera_terms.use_when: Show posture, clothing or full-body gesture.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: full body shot, head to toe

camera_terms.definition: A framing that cuts a standing subject around the knees.
camera_terms.visual_effect: It balances readable gesture with facial and environmental information.
camera_terms.use_when: Show body language while keeping the face important.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that cuts a standing subject around mid-thigh, historically leaving a holster visible.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Hands, hips and facial expression share emphasis.
camera_terms.use_when: Feature hand action, stance or a waist-level prop.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that generally shows a person from the waist upward.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Expression and upper-body gesture receive balanced attention.
camera_terms.use_when: Use for dialogue, interviews or character interaction.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that generally shows a person from the chest or shoulders upward.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The face dominates while posture and context remain partially visible.
camera_terms.use_when: Prioritise expression without losing all surroundings.

camera_terms.definition: A framing in which a face or similarly sized subject detail fills most of the image.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Fine expression and texture become visually dominant.
camera_terms.use_when: Make an emotion or important object unmistakable.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that fills the image with a face from roughly forehead to chin.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Facial micro-expression appears with very little contextual space.
camera_terms.use_when: Heighten a reaction without isolating only one feature.

camera_terms.definition: A framing that isolates a very small feature such as an eye, mouth or mechanism.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Texture and minute detail become abstractly large.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal a clue, sensation or precise material detail.

camera_terms.definition: A tightly framed view of an object or action detail intended to carry specific information.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A prop, text or small action becomes unmissable.
camera_terms.use_when: Clarify a story-critical object within a larger scene.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: tight insert shot of key object

camera_terms.definition: A composition that leaves little unused space between the subject and frame edges.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject feels visually confined and immediately dominant.
camera_terms.use_when: Increase pressure or remove distracting context.

camera_terms.definition: A composition that leaves generous space around the principal subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Surroundings and empty areas gain visual weight.
camera_terms.use_when: Make context or isolation part of the image.

camera_terms.definition: A frame whose width is greater than its height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Horizontal relationships and lateral environments receive more room.
camera_terms.use_when: Show groups, landscapes or side-to-side spatial relationships.

camera_terms.definition: A frame whose height is greater than its width.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Vertical bodies and height relationships fill the image efficiently.
camera_terms.use_when: Create portraits, fashion images or mobile-first compositions.

camera_terms.definition: The optical axis views the subject from approximately the subject’s eye level without pronounced up- or down-tilt.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Vertical proportions appear familiar and minimally judged.
camera_terms.use_when: Present a subject without imposing obvious dominance.

camera_terms.definition: The camera looks downward at the subject from above its reference height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The top surfaces become visible and the subject appears reduced.
camera_terms.use_when: Diminish a subject or clarify floor-plan relationships.

camera_terms.definition: The camera looks upward at the subject from below its reference height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Lower surfaces dominate and the subject rises against the background.
camera_terms.use_when: Make a person or structure feel imposing.

camera_terms.definition: The optical axis points almost vertically downward onto the scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Depth collapses into plan-like shapes and spatial patterns.
camera_terms.use_when: Show layouts, choreography, food or graphic arrangements.

camera_terms.definition: The camera views the scene from a very high position at a downward oblique angle.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Subjects become small within a readable expanse of terrain.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal geography while retaining some horizon-facing surfaces.

camera_terms.definition: The camera views upward from at or near ground level.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground forms loom and vertical convergence becomes pronounced.
camera_terms.use_when: Exaggerate height or monumentalise a subject.

camera_terms.definition: The camera is rolled so the horizon or verticals are intentionally diagonal.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame loses normal gravitational alignment.
camera_terms.use_when: Signal disorder, danger or psychological imbalance.

camera_terms.definition: The camera faces the front plane of the subject nearly square-on.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Symmetry and direct shape recognition are strengthened.
camera_terms.use_when: Show identity, geometry or direct presentation.

camera_terms.definition: The camera sees both the front and one side of the subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Form gains dimensionality without losing facial or object identity.
camera_terms.use_when: Create a dimensional portrait or product view.

camera_terms.definition: The camera views the subject from approximately ninety degrees to its frontal axis.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Silhouette, nose line and lateral gesture become prominent.
camera_terms.use_when: Emphasise outline, gaze direction or side-on action.

camera_terms.definition: The camera sees the back and one side of the subject.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Identity is partly withheld while direction into space remains visible.
camera_terms.use_when: Follow attention toward a scene without using a full rear view.

camera_terms.definition: The camera faces the back plane of the subject nearly square-on.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Facial information disappears and the subject’s destination gains emphasis.
camera_terms.use_when: Align the viewer with where the subject is looking.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera body is positioned at or only centimetres above the supporting surface.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Near foreground objects enlarge and the ground plane recedes strongly.
camera_terms.use_when: Emphasise terrain, feet, small subjects or towering structures.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is placed around a standing subject’s ankle height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Feet and lower foreground gain prominence while some ground separation remains.
camera_terms.use_when: Feature footwear, steps or low obstacles.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is placed around a standing subject’s knee height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Legs and low furniture become visually assertive without an extreme ground view.
camera_terms.use_when: Show movement-ready posture or a child-scale environment.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is placed around a standing subject’s hip height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Hands, waist and nearby surfaces sit near the optical centre.
camera_terms.use_when: Prioritise handwork, counters or waist-level action.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is placed around the subject’s waist level.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Upper and lower body proportions remain balanced with a subtly low viewpoint.
camera_terms.use_when: Photograph seated groups, tables or full figures without eye-height formality.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is placed around the subject’s chest height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The torso aligns centrally and facial perspective remains restrained.
camera_terms.use_when: Create natural portraits slightly below eye level.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is placed around the subject’s shoulder height.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewpoint approaches conversational height while retaining a small upward bias.
camera_terms.use_when: Frame standing dialogue or documentary portraits.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The lens entrance pupil is positioned near the subject’s eyes.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Facial proportions and interpersonal height cues appear familiar.
camera_terms.use_when: Make portraits and conversations feel natural.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is positioned above the subject’s head but not necessarily directly overhead.
camera_terms.visual_effect: More hair, shoulders and surrounding floor enter the image.
camera_terms.use_when: Look over crowds, reveal working surfaces or reduce subject dominance.

camera_terms.category: Camera height and position relative to subject
camera_terms.definition: The camera is physically positioned directly above the subject or scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Objects align against the ground plane with minimal lateral occlusion.
camera_terms.use_when: Create maps, layouts, flat lays or geometric scenes.

camera_terms.definition: A frame contains one principal human subject without another comparably important person.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Attention concentrates on one character’s expression and body language.
camera_terms.use_when: Give one person uncontested narrative emphasis.

camera_terms.definition: A frame composes two principal subjects together.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Relationship, distance and relative status become visible at once.
camera_terms.use_when: Show interaction without cutting between individuals.

camera_terms.definition: A frame composes three principal subjects together.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A triangular or linear relationship structure becomes readable.
camera_terms.use_when: Show a three-person exchange or hierarchy.

camera_terms.definition: A frame contains four or more principal people as a coordinated visual group.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Collective arrangement and internal hierarchy dominate individual detail.
camera_terms.use_when: Present a team, family, cast or gathering.

camera_terms.definition: The camera frames a subject beyond the partial head or shoulder of another person in the foreground.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Foreground overlap establishes conversational geography and affiliation.
camera_terms.use_when: Anchor dialogue to one participant’s physical viewpoint.

camera_terms.definition: A single-subject framing retains a small out-of-focus portion of another person at a frame edge.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The featured subject remains dominant while the partner’s presence persists.
camera_terms.use_when: Preserve relational context in a reaction portrait.

camera_terms.definition: A single-subject framing excludes other scene partners from the visible frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject’s reaction is isolated from conversational foreground elements.
camera_terms.use_when: Give an individual an undistracted reaction image.

camera_terms.definition: Two subjects are framed together largely in opposing profile.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Faces and the space between them form a graphic relational axis.
camera_terms.use_when: Stage dialogue, a kiss or a face-off symmetrically.

camera_terms.definition: Subjects are blocked at deliberately different distances from the camera within one composition.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Near-far scale differences create layered spatial hierarchy.
camera_terms.use_when: Show simultaneous relationships across foreground and background.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: subjects staged across foreground and background

camera_terms.definition: A nearer object partially blocks the principal subject or scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewer sees through or around an intervening layer.
camera_terms.use_when: Suggest observation, enclosure or physical depth.

camera_terms.definition: The subject’s eyes look directly into the camera lens.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The gaze meets the viewer without visible angular offset.
camera_terms.use_when: Create direct address, fashion impact or self-aware portraiture.

camera_terms.definition: The subject looks toward a point outside the frame rather than into the lens.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Gaze direction activates unseen space beyond an edge.
camera_terms.use_when: Imply another person, object or event outside the image.

camera_terms.definition: The frame is divided into thirds horizontally and vertically and key elements are placed near the resulting lines or intersections.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject sits off-centre within an easily read spatial balance.
camera_terms.use_when: Create a clear composition with room for context or gaze.

camera_terms.definition: The primary subject or dominant axis is placed at the geometric centre of the frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Visual weight becomes immediate, frontal and stable.
camera_terms.use_when: Emphasise symmetry, iconography or direct address.

camera_terms.definition: Visual elements mirror or closely balance across a central axis.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame appears ordered and deliberately controlled.
camera_terms.use_when: Highlight architecture, ceremony or rigid control.

camera_terms.definition: Unequal elements are arranged so their differing visual weights still stabilise the frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The image feels balanced without mirroring or centring.
camera_terms.use_when: Create tension and interest while retaining coherence.

camera_terms.definition: Visible lines or aligned forms direct attention toward a chosen subject or depth point.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The eye follows a controlled route through the image.
camera_terms.use_when: Guide attention through roads, rails, shadows or architecture.

camera_terms.definition: Dominant subjects or structural lines run diagonally across the frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The image gains directional force and reduced static balance.
camera_terms.use_when: Add movement-like tension to a static image.

camera_terms.definition: Three dominant points or subjects form an implied triangle within the frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The eye circulates among three anchors while the base supplies stability.
camera_terms.use_when: Organise three people or major shapes coherently.

camera_terms.definition: A visible foreground or architectural boundary encloses the principal subject inside the outer image frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Nested borders concentrate attention and add depth.
camera_terms.use_when: Use doors, windows, mirrors or foliage to isolate a subject.

camera_terms.definition: A substantial area around the subject contains little visual detail or competing information.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject gains emphasis through surrounding emptiness.
camera_terms.use_when: Leave room for gaze, text or environmental scale.

camera_terms.definition: Distinct visual elements occupy near, middle and far depth zones.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The image reads as a layered volume rather than a flat plane.
camera_terms.use_when: Build spatial depth in landscapes, interiors or ensembles.

camera_terms.definition: An odd number of similar subjects is arranged as the principal grouping.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The grouping resists simple pairing and often centres one element.
camera_terms.use_when: Compose flowers, products or small groups with visual variety.

camera_terms.definition: Repeated shapes, colours or intervals form a dominant organising structure.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Rhythm and regularity spread across the frame.
camera_terms.use_when: Emphasise architecture, crowds, products or natural texture.

camera_terms.definition: Lines or repeated elements spread outward from or converge toward a central point.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Attention is pulled strongly toward a hub.
camera_terms.use_when: Compose wheels, staircases, flowers or converging groups.

camera_terms.definition: A subject boundary or leading line follows an S-shaped path through the frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The gaze moves gradually between foreground and distance.
camera_terms.use_when: Guide the eye through roads, bodies, rivers or fabric.

camera_terms.definition: Parallel receding lines converge toward one dominant vanishing point.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Depth becomes graphic, centred and strongly directional.
camera_terms.use_when: Show corridors, roads or architecture with forceful depth.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: Only a narrow distance range around the focus plane is acceptably sharp.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject separates from a blurred foreground and background.
camera_terms.use_when: Isolate one subject or suppress distracting context.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: shallow depth of field, sharp subject

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: Near, middle and distant scene elements are all rendered acceptably sharp.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Multiple depth layers remain simultaneously readable.
camera_terms.use_when: Let viewers inspect relationships across the whole scene.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: deep focus from foreground to background

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: Focus is deliberately restricted to one chosen subject while competing planes remain soft.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A precise visual priority emerges within a layered scene.
camera_terms.use_when: Direct the eye to one face, object or detail.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: The lens is focused at the distance that extends acceptable sharpness from roughly half that distance to infinity.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Maximum practical near-to-far sharpness is obtained for a chosen aperture.
camera_terms.use_when: Photograph landscapes, streets or fast scenes without refocusing.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: Focus is preset so an anticipated distance interval falls within acceptable depth of field.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Subjects entering the chosen distance zone appear sharp without visible focus searching.
camera_terms.use_when: Work quickly in street, reportage or unpredictable situations.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: zone focus with broad sharp range

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: The focus setting places very distant subjects at the image plane.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Distant landscapes, stars or horizons become sharp while near objects soften.
camera_terms.use_when: Photograph celestial or very distant subjects.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: The focus distance is set extremely close for high subject magnification.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Tiny textures fill the frame and depth of field becomes very narrow.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal small products, organisms or surface detail.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: The lens plane is tilted relative to the sensor so the focus plane rotates through the scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A diagonal or receding surface can remain sharp while adjacent regions blur.
camera_terms.use_when: Align focus with a tabletop, landscape plane or selective wedge.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: Multiple fixed-camera exposures focused at different distances are combined into one image.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Extreme near-to-far sharpness appears beyond a single exposure’s depth of field.
camera_terms.use_when: Render macro products, specimens or landscapes entirely sharp.

camera_terms.category: Focus, depth of field and plane control
camera_terms.definition: Focus is placed with maximum precision on the image’s most important fine detail.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The chosen feature appears decisively sharp against any softer regions.
camera_terms.use_when: Make eyes, text or product details incontrovertibly sharp.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: The sensor or film receives less exposure than a neutral rendering would require.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Midtones and shadows darken and may lose detail.
camera_terms.use_when: Protect highlights or create a deliberately dark image.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: The sensor or film receives more exposure than a neutral rendering would require.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Highlights brighten, wash out or clip while shadows lift.
camera_terms.use_when: Create an airy wash or sacrifice highlights intentionally.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Exposure is set to retain texture in the brightest important region.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Bright areas keep detail while midtones and shadows fall darker.
camera_terms.use_when: Preserve windows, skies, flames or pale clothing.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Exposure is set to retain texture in the darkest important region.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Shadow detail opens while bright areas approach clipping.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal dark interiors, faces in shade or low-key textures.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Exposure is based on a bright background so the unlit foreground subject records very dark.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The subject becomes a simplified outline against a luminous field.
camera_terms.use_when: Hide identity while emphasising pose or shape.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Lighting and exposure place most tonal values in the bright range with limited dark shadow.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The frame appears luminous, clean and low in dark-area weight.
camera_terms.use_when: Create beauty, comedy, advertising or clean product imagery.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Lighting and exposure place most tonal values in the dark range with selective highlights.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Large shadow areas surround a few bright forms.
camera_terms.use_when: Create noir, horror or sculptural portraiture.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Lighting or exposure creates a large tonal separation between bright and dark areas.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Edges and shapes read boldly while transitional midtones diminish.
camera_terms.use_when: Emphasise structure, conflict or hard light.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: Lighting or exposure keeps highlights and shadows within a relatively narrow tonal range.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Tonal transitions appear soft and detail remains open across the frame.
camera_terms.use_when: Create flattering portraits, misty scenes or flexible tonal capture.

camera_terms.category: Exposure, contrast and lighting-driven camera choices
camera_terms.definition: The camera uses a high sensitivity setting that requires less light for a given exposure.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Noise or grain increases and very low-light detail becomes visible.
camera_terms.use_when: Work in dim light or deliberately add coarse texture.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: A digital sensor approximately matches the 36 by 24 millimetre still-photography frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: For equivalent framing and aperture it supports shallower depth of field than smaller formats.
camera_terms.use_when: Seek broad lens availability and strong subject separation.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: A digital sensor is larger than the 35mm full-frame still format.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Fine detail, smooth tonal transitions and shallow equivalent depth of field are emphasised.
camera_terms.use_when: Create premium portrait, fashion, landscape or product imagery.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: A digital cinema sensor uses an imaging area comparable to the Super 35 motion-picture frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The field of view is narrower than full frame for the same focal length and lens character feels conventionally cinematic.
camera_terms.use_when: Match established cinema lens coverage and depth rendering.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: The image is photochemically recorded on 35mm colour-negative stock.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Organic grain, highlight roll-off and stock-dependent colour texture appear.
camera_terms.use_when: Seek a classic photochemical cinema or still-photo character.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: The image is photochemically recorded on 16mm or Super 16 colour-negative stock.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Grain is more apparent and fine detail coarser than comparable 35mm capture.
camera_terms.use_when: Create tactile reportage, period or independent-film texture.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: A tungsten-balanced ISO 500 KODAK VISION3 colour-negative stock records the image photochemically.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Visible fine grain, broad latitude and warm practical-light colour response shape the frame.
camera_terms.use_when: Shoot low-light interiors or emulate contemporary film-origin cinema.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: The image is framed at approximately 1.37 units wide for every unit high.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The near-square frame concentrates vertical bodies and central staging.
camera_terms.use_when: Evoke early sound cinema or contain lateral space.

camera_terms.category: Format, aspect ratio, film stock and capture medium
camera_terms.definition: The image is framed at approximately 2.39 units wide for every unit high.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Wide lateral relationships expand while vertical space is reduced.
camera_terms.use_when: Stage ensembles, landscapes or strong left-to-right relationships.

camera_terms.definition: A usually wide static view identifies the location and spatial context for a subject or scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Geography and environment become immediately legible.
camera_terms.use_when: Introduce where subsequent action or imagery belongs.

camera_terms.definition: A single comprehensive framing contains the principal subjects and usable spatial action of a scene.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The complete relationship and geography remain visible in one view.
camera_terms.use_when: Cover an ensemble or staged scene comprehensively.
camera_terms.prompt_fragment: static master shot of full scene

camera_terms.definition: The camera occupies the visual position of a character or observer.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The viewer sees the scene from an implied participant’s location.
camera_terms.use_when: Reveal what a character directly sees.

camera_terms.definition: Performers and objects are arranged as a deliberately pictorial scene within a largely frontal static frame.
camera_terms.visual_effect: The image reads like a staged painting with simultaneous details.
camera_terms.use_when: Present an ensemble, ritual or symbolic mise-en-scène.

camera_terms.definition: Objects are arranged on a flat surface and photographed from directly overhead.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Depth is suppressed into a clean graphic inventory of shapes.
camera_terms.use_when: Photograph food, fashion, tools or product collections.

camera_terms.definition: Subjects at different distances are aligned so their apparent scales create a false spatial relationship.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Objects appear impossibly large, small, touching or supporting one another.
camera_terms.use_when: Create in-camera scale illusions without compositing.

camera_terms.definition: The principal subject is viewed partly or entirely through a reflective surface.
camera_terms.visual_effect: A second image plane duplicates, reframes or conceals the subject.
camera_terms.use_when: Show identity, off-axis space or layered information.

camera_terms.definition: A subject or product is given a polished, dominant presentation designed as the image’s primary statement.
camera_terms.visual_effect: Lighting, angle and negative space make the subject appear iconic and advertisement-ready.
camera_terms.use_when: Create campaign art, product advertising or a defining character image.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A rectilinear focal length substantially shorter than the format’s normal lens, commonly below 24mm full-frame equivalent.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It covers a very wide field and exaggerates near–far scale when the camera is placed close.
lens_terms.use_when: Make confined spaces, foregrounds or vast architecture feel deep.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A focal length shorter than normal, commonly around 24–35mm full-frame equivalent.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It includes broad surroundings and strengthens depth when used near the subject.
lens_terms.use_when: Balance an important foreground subject with substantial environment.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A mildly wide focal length near 35mm full-frame equivalent.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It gives environmental context with less edge stretching than shorter lenses.
lens_terms.use_when: Create reportage, street or environmental portraits.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A focal length near the format diagonal, commonly 40–60mm on full frame.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The field of view and spatial scaling appear comparatively neutral.
lens_terms.use_when: Avoid an obviously wide or telephoto signature.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A focal length moderately longer than normal, commonly 70–105mm full-frame equivalent.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It narrows the field and supports flattering portrait distance with strong background separation.
lens_terms.use_when: Photograph portraits and details without extreme compression.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A focal length around 120–200mm full-frame equivalent.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It isolates distant subjects and makes separated depth planes appear closer when framing is matched.
lens_terms.use_when: Shoot stage, sport, landscape details or compressed portraits.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A focal length around 300–500mm full-frame equivalent.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It produces a narrow field, strong magnification and dense apparent layering from distant camera positions.
lens_terms.use_when: Isolate wildlife, sport or landscape layers from far away.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A focal length of roughly 600mm or longer on full frame.
lens_terms.visual_effect: A very narrow field enlarges remote subjects and strongly layers distant backgrounds.
lens_terms.use_when: Fill the frame with wildlife, aircraft, sport or celestial subjects.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A format-relative range, often 70–135mm full-frame equivalent, commonly selected for head-and-shoulders portraits.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Working distance reduces near-feature exaggeration and helps separate the background.
lens_terms.use_when: Create conventional beauty, editorial or corporate portraits.

lens_terms.category: Focal length classes and what each does to perspective
lens_terms.definition: A group of focal lengths, commonly 50–200mm, offered in lenses capable of high reproduction ratios.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Working distance and background angle vary while tiny subjects can fill the image.
lens_terms.use_when: Choose practical working distance for products, insects or copy work.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 14mm rectilinear lens on full frame provides an extremely wide fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Foreground scale and edge stretching become conspicuous while interiors feel expanded.
lens_terms.use_when: Show cramped architecture, dramatic skies or exaggerated foregrounds.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: An 18mm lens on full frame provides an ultra-wide fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It captures broad surroundings with strong depth but less extremity than 14mm.
lens_terms.use_when: Shoot interiors, landscapes or close environmental action.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 24mm lens on full frame provides a classic wide fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Near subjects feel prominent while substantial environment remains visible.
lens_terms.use_when: Create environmental portraits, architecture or dynamic wide images.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 28mm lens on full frame provides a moderately strong wide fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It feels immersive and documentary-like without the extremity of an ultrawide.
lens_terms.use_when: Photograph streets, groups and contextual portraits from nearby.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 35mm lens on full frame provides a mild wide fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It includes environment while keeping people comparatively natural near the centre.
lens_terms.use_when: Make environmental portraits, reportage or small-room scenes.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 50mm lens on full frame provides a normal fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Spatial relationships appear neutral with moderate background separation at wide apertures.
lens_terms.use_when: Create general-purpose portraits, details or low-light stills.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: An 85mm lens on full frame provides a short-telephoto fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Portraits gain flattering working distance and smooth background separation.
lens_terms.use_when: Shoot head-and-shoulders portraits and beauty work.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 100mm macro lens combines short-telephoto framing with close focus near life-size reproduction.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Small subjects fill the frame from a comfortable working distance with very shallow depth.
lens_terms.use_when: Photograph products, food, insects, eyes or textures.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 135mm lens on full frame provides a medium-telephoto fixed field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Faces and distant backgrounds appear strongly separated and spatially layered.
lens_terms.use_when: Create compressed outdoor portraits or isolate stage details.

lens_terms.category: Specific named focal lengths and their signature look
lens_terms.definition: A 200mm lens on full frame provides a narrow medium-telephoto field of view.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Remote details enlarge and distant depth planes appear densely stacked.
lens_terms.use_when: Isolate sport, wildlife, landscapes or candid subjects.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: The lens iris is set to its largest available opening.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Exposure increases, depth of field narrows and optical character is least corrected.
lens_terms.use_when: Work in low light or isolate a subject strongly.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: The iris is set several stops smaller than the lens maximum.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Depth of field increases and aperture-shaped highlights may become more defined.
lens_terms.use_when: Keep multiple planes sharp or control bright light.
lens_terms.prompt_fragment: lens stopped down for deep focus

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus detail is rendered with low-edged, gradual tonal transitions.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Background clutter dissolves into soft shapes rather than busy contours.
lens_terms.use_when: Create flattering portraits or premium product imagery.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus point highlights render as approximately circular discs near the image centre.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Background lights become soft round orbs.
lens_terms.use_when: Use practical lights to create clean luminous separation.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus point highlights take the polygonal shape of the partially closed iris.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Blur discs show visible straight edges and geometric repetition.
lens_terms.use_when: Make the iris-blade signature visible in background lights.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus highlights near the frame edges are clipped into oval cat-eye shapes by the lens barrel.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Blur discs stretch tangentially around the image perimeter.
lens_terms.use_when: Add edge character to night portraits at wide aperture.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Off-axis blur and field curvature organise background detail into a rotational pattern around the centre.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The soft background appears to spiral around the sharp subject.
lens_terms.use_when: Give portraits an unmistakable vintage optical signature.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus highlights have bright defined rims and relatively dim centres.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Background points become luminous outlined circles resembling bubbles.
lens_terms.use_when: Create distinctive vintage macro or portrait backgrounds.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus highlight discs contain concentric internal rings caused by fine aspherical-surface structure.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Blur circles show visible nested texture rather than smooth fill.
lens_terms.use_when: Deliberately evoke modern aspherical lens artefacts.

lens_terms.category: Aperture, bokeh and out-of-focus rendering
lens_terms.definition: Out-of-focus detail retains strong edges, doubling or high-frequency texture.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Backgrounds compete more visibly with the sharp subject.
lens_terms.use_when: Seek a raw vintage or deliberately unsettled background.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: A lens has one fixed focal length and no focal-length zoom mechanism.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Its chosen field of view remains fixed and often permits a faster, smaller or more consistent optical design.
lens_terms.use_when: Prioritise speed, compactness or a specific focal signature.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: A lens can vary focal length continuously across a stated range while remaining mounted.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The fixed frame inherits whichever field of view the lens is set to, with possible zoom-design rendering traits.
lens_terms.use_when: Work quickly across multiple framings or inaccessible positions.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: Cylindrical optical power compresses a wider horizontal field onto the capture area for later desqueezing.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The image can show oval bokeh, horizontal flare and different horizontal versus vertical perspective rendering.
lens_terms.use_when: Create a widescreen cinema signature with characteristic artefacts.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: The lens uses rotationally symmetric imaging optics without anamorphic horizontal squeeze.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Geometry and bokeh remain similar in horizontal and vertical directions.
lens_terms.use_when: Avoid anamorphic squeeze and directional artefacts.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: A lens is corrected to focus at high reproduction ratios, commonly reaching 1:1 on the sensor.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Small subjects fill the image with high close-range detail and narrow depth of field.
lens_terms.use_when: Photograph insects, products, documents or textures.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: The lens can tilt and shift relative to the sensor while the camera body remains fixed.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Shift controls convergence and tilt rotates the plane of focus.
lens_terms.use_when: Correct architecture or create selective-plane effects.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: An extreme-wide lens uses a deliberately non-rectilinear projection.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Straight lines away from the centre bow dramatically and the field may approach 180 degrees.
lens_terms.use_when: Create immersive distortion or fit an enormous view into one frame.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: A lens uses a notably thin, compact barrel relative to its image format.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The optical look is focal-length dependent, while the small build encourages unobtrusive close placement.
lens_terms.use_when: Keep a camera discreet for travel, street or compact setups.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: A telephoto lens folds the light path using mirrors as well as refractive elements.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It gives strong telephoto compression with fixed aperture and ring-shaped out-of-focus highlights.
lens_terms.use_when: Obtain long reach or distinctive doughnut bokeh.

lens_terms.category: Lens types and physical builds
lens_terms.definition: A long narrow relay lens places a small front element close to or inside confined subjects while the camera remains farther away.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The view can travel visually through miniature spaces with extreme close focus and unusually deep perspective.
lens_terms.use_when: Photograph food, miniatures, products or inaccessible interiors.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Magnification decreases toward the frame edges so straight lines bow outward.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The centre bulges visually and edge geometry curves away.
lens_terms.use_when: Exaggerate space or evoke action cameras and vintage wide lenses.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Magnification increases toward the frame edges so straight lines bow inward.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Frame edges appear pulled toward the corners.
lens_terms.use_when: Invoke imperfect telephoto or zoom optics deliberately.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Different wavelengths fail to converge at the same point or magnification.
lens_terms.visual_effect: High-contrast edges acquire coloured fringes, often cyan, magenta, red or blue.
lens_terms.use_when: Add vintage, lo-fi or stressed-optics character.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Marginal and central rays from spherical surfaces focus at different longitudinal positions.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Wide-open detail blooms and focus transitions or bokeh edges become characterful.
lens_terms.use_when: Soften portraits or create distinctive foreground and background blur.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Off-axis point sources are imaged asymmetrically because rays at different pupil zones magnify differently.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Edge lights stretch into comet-like wings or tails.
lens_terms.use_when: Give night lights, stars or vintage corners a smeared signature.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Tangential and sagittal detail at the same off-axis point focus on different planes.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Edge detail stretches in different directions and fine texture loses uniform sharpness.
lens_terms.use_when: Create directional corner softness or characterful bokeh.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: The lens forms its sharpest image on a curved surface rather than a flat sensor plane.
lens_terms.visual_effect: A flat subject cannot remain uniformly sharp from centre to edges at one focus setting.
lens_terms.use_when: Create centre emphasis, swirly backgrounds or vintage edge softness.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: The lens transmits less illumination toward the image corners than at the centre.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Corners darken and attention gathers toward the middle.
lens_terms.use_when: Focus attention or evoke vintage and wide-open optics.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Stray light scatters broadly inside the lens without forming a distinct source image.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Contrast falls and highlights spread into a milky coloured wash.
lens_terms.use_when: Soften a backlit image or suggest atmosphere and memory.

lens_terms.category: Optical characteristics, aberrations and flaws used deliberately
lens_terms.definition: Reflections between optical surfaces form distinct images of a bright source or aperture.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Coloured discs, polygons or arcs repeat across the frame.
lens_terms.use_when: Make a visible light source feel intense or cinematic.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A neutral filter reduces transmitted light approximately evenly across visible wavelengths.
lens_terms.visual_effect: It permits wider apertures or longer exposures without changing nominal colour.
lens_terms.use_when: Control exposure while preserving the chosen aperture look.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A filter transitions from neutral density to clear across part of its surface.
lens_terms.visual_effect: A bright region such as a sky darkens while the rest remains relatively unchanged.
lens_terms.use_when: Hold sky detail against a darker landscape in one exposure.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A linear polarizer followed by a quarter-wave layer selectively transmits light orientation while remaining compatible with modern metering systems.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Reflections on non-metallic surfaces reduce and blue skies or foliage can deepen.
lens_terms.use_when: Control glare on water, glass, leaves or painted surfaces.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A front filter scatters a controlled portion of image-forming light.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Highlights bloom, microcontrast falls and skin detail softens while gross focus remains.
lens_terms.use_when: Take digital sharpness off portraits or create halation around lights.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: Etched or embedded lines diffract bright point sources into defined rays.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Lights acquire repeated star-shaped spikes whose count follows the filter pattern.
lens_terms.use_when: Stylise jewellery, night lights or polished highlights.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A positive supplementary lens mounted in front of the taking lens shortens its minimum focus distance.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The camera can magnify nearer subjects, often with softer edges and reduced working distance.
lens_terms.use_when: Make a non-macro or anamorphic lens focus closer.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A partial positive lens covers only part of the taking lens so a near region and distant region can be focused together.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Two separated depth zones appear sharp with a visible soft transition boundary.
lens_terms.use_when: Hold an extreme foreground detail and background subject sharp together.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: Fine parallel structures in a front filter spread point lights along one axis.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Bright sources produce long directional flare streaks, usually horizontal.
lens_terms.use_when: Simulate or intensify an anamorphic-style flare.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A coloured optical filter changes the spectral balance of light before it reaches the capture medium.
lens_terms.visual_effect: The entire image shifts warmer, cooler or toward a compensating hue.
lens_terms.use_when: Match daylight and tungsten sources or create an in-camera colour bias.

lens_terms.category: Filters and front-of-lens attachments
lens_terms.definition: A coloured front filter selectively transmits wavelengths before monochrome capture or conversion.
lens_terms.visual_effect: Different scene colours separate into lighter or darker grey values, with red filters strongly darkening blue skies.
lens_terms.use_when: Control tonal separation in monochrome landscapes or portraits.

notes: Researched against official references from Canon, Nikon, ARRI, Kodak, ZEISS, Tiffen, Adobe and Google. Focal length directly controls field of view; apparent perspective changes described here assume the camera is repositioned to maintain comparable subject framing. Reliability is a qualitative cross-model estimate as of 2026-08-11: common semantic descriptions rate higher than exact optical simulations. Sources: Canon focal length https://www.canon-europe.com/pro/infobank/understanding-focal-length/ ; Nikon composition https://www.nikonusa.com/learn-and-explore/c/tips-and-techniques/when-center-composition-can-elevate-a-portrait ; ARRI formats https://www.arri.com/en/cine-systems/cine-cameras/amira ; Kodak glossary https://www.kodak.com/en/motion/page/glossary-of-motion-picture-terms/ ; ZEISS lens characteristics https://www.zeiss.com/photonics-and-optics/us/cinematography/cincraft/lenscore.html ; Tiffen split diopter https://tiffen.com/products/138mm-split-field-diopter ; Google Imagen prompting https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/a-developers-guide-to-imagen-3-on-vertex-ai
